full_text_en:
Houyingzi Supply and Marketing Cooperative v. Tiesanzhong Frozen Food Machinery Sales Department — product liability dispute

Plaintiff: Houyingzi Supply and Marketing Cooperative, Suburb of Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal representative: Liu Yu, Director of the Cooperative.

Agents ad litem: Wang Jiali and Wang Wenjiang, lawyers from Donghe District Law Office, Baotou City.

Defendant: Frozen Food Machinery Sales Department, Baotou Railway No. 3 Middle School.

Legal representative: Meng Zhiyuan, Manager of the Sales Department.

Agent ad litem: Wang Wei, lawyer from Ulanqab League Law Office.

Agent ad litem: Liang Deqing, lawyer from Baotou City Law Office.

The plaintiff, Houyingzi Supply and Marketing Cooperative, Suburb of Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, filed an action against the defendant, Frozen Food Machinery Sales Department, Baotou Railway No. 3 Middle School, in the Donghe District People's Court of Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, regarding a product liability dispute. The court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and, after public trial, found the following:

On July 13, 1988, the plaintiff, Houyingzi Supply and Marketing Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as Houyingzi Cooperative), purchased one "Baita" brand freezer produced by Subei Freezer Factory from the defendant, Frozen Food Machinery Sales Department, Baotou Railway No. 3 Middle School (hereinafter referred to as Tiesanzhong Machinery Sales Department). On August 8 of the same year, the defendant sent personnel to commission the freezer, after which it was put into use. At about 6:00 a.m. on August 31, Wang Wenhai, an employee of the plaintiff, grasped the handle of the freezer to open the door and retrieve food, when he was electrocuted and died because the cabinet body was electrified. After appraisal by the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Standard Bureau: During operation of the freezer, due to poor contact in one phase of the incoming terminal of the contactor in the magnetic starter, causing an open circuit in that phase, the motor operated on two phases, and the current increased. At this point, the thermal relay should have acted under the increased current in the main circuit to cut off the power supply. However, because the freezer should have been equipped with a 3.5 ampere magnetic starter but was incorrectly fitted with an 8 ampere magnetic starter, and no screw-type fuse was installed in the main circuit, and no screw-type fuse or intermediate relay was installed in the control circuit, when the machine malfunctioned, the motor was not protected and continued to operate until it burned out, causing the motor casing and the freezer cabinet body to become electrified. Additionally, there was no grounding wire, resulting in Wang Wenhai's electrocution when he touched the metal cabinet handle to open the freezer door. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the defendant to refund the purchase price of the non-conforming product, compensate for business interruption losses, and bear the bereavement expenses for Wang Wenhai. The defendant argued that the freezer they sold was a certified product inspected by the Jiangsu Provincial Standard Bureau; on August 8, their technicians commissioned and adjusted it, and it operated normally; moreover, the plaintiff had used it for 23 days with good performance. Wang Wenhai's electrocution was caused by the plaintiff's improper installation, so they should not bear economic liability.

The Donghe District People's Court found after trial: Although the "Baita" brand freezer produced by Subei Freezer Factory and sold by the defendant had a product quality certificate issued by the Jiangsu Provincial Standard Bureau, appraisal by the relevant authorities confirmed that the freezer sold by the defendant to the plaintiff was indeed a non-conforming product. Because the magnetic starter was incorrectly installed, the current increased, the motor was not protected and burned out, causing the motor and freezer cabinet body to become electrified. As for the fact that the malfunction occurred only after 23 days of use, under normal conditions, even with the incorrectly installed magnetic starter, the motor could still operate normally for a certain period. Once the motor malfunctioned, the above situation would arise. As for the grounding wire issue, even if the plaintiff had installed a grounding wire on the freezer, once the motor and cabinet body became electrified, the excessive current would still have caused serious consequences. The above circumstances were the cause of Wang Wenhai's electrocution. Article 122 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a defective product causes property damage or physical injury to others, the manufacturer or seller of the product shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law." The defendant should bear liability for Wang Wenhai's death caused by the non-conforming product. Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "If a citizen's body is injured, compensation shall be paid for medical expenses, reduced income due to lost work time, and living subsidies for the disabled; if death is caused, funeral expenses, necessary living expenses for the decedent's dependents, and other such expenses shall also be paid." Article 15 of the Regulations on the Responsibility for the Quality of Industrial Products promulgated by the State Council provides that if a product sold by a distribution enterprise is non-conforming, the distribution enterprise shall be responsible for repairing, replacing, or returning the product for the user and for compensating actual economic losses. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim for compensation for economic losses and funeral expenses for the decedent is justified and should be supported. Accordingly, on February 24, 1989, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The plaintiff shall return the freezer purchased from the defendant, and the defendant shall refund the plaintiff the purchase price, freight, and compensate the plaintiff for business interruption losses, totaling 7,900 yuan;

2. The defendant shall pay the plaintiff funeral expenses for the decedent, living expenses for the decedent's dependents, and bereavement compensation, totaling 13,986.90 yuan;

3. The defendant shall pay the decedent's family members' lost work time, transportation expenses, etc., totaling 4,152.03 yuan.

Appraisal fees of 800 yuan shall be paid by the defendant.

Court costs of 290 yuan: the defendant shall bear 232 yuan, and the plaintiff shall bear 58 yuan.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed.
